$comment: Hard gate for config/litellm-proxy.yaml (fleet-ops#8653). Nish 2026-09-28: no benching unless he says so. A failed row is never taken out of rotation: no bench list. Row cooldown_time: <=900 s is for ordinary transients. Values over 900 s, up to the 86400 s cap, are reserved for rows with a named, self-refilling wall (a daily or monthly quota that outlasts 900 s) - the row stays live, parked, and re-probes itself; each such row cites its issue in a comment (fleet-ops#8398/#9075). A row on openrouter.ai/api/v1 must set model_info.allowed_fails_policy.RateLimitErrorAllowedFails: 0, because its 429s are OpenRouter's named daily free-tier wall and the row has to park on the first one (fleet-ops#9248). Router-level cooldown_time holds a failed row for at most 60 s. Every model_list row must declare its cache capability: model_info.supports_prompt_caching (boolean) and model_info.cache_proof (non-empty string, date plus measured cached tokens or a doc link), because ~0% cache-read on four provider groups was 70% of uncached router tokens and no rule forced a new seat to say which case it is (fleet-ops#9365). A worker-group row whose supports_prompt_caching is false must set litellm_params.order: 2 so long sessions fall to it only as overflow (order filtering is applied after the cooldown filter in LiteLLM v1.98.0 router.py, proven by tests/test_router_order2_overflow.py). router_settings.redis_host, redis_port and redis_password (os.environ/REDIS_PASSWORD) are required and redis_url is forbidden (v1.98.0 drops the password when redis_url is set; the cache has requirepass): session_affinity pins live in the Router cache, and without Redis each of the proxy's 2 worker processes keeps its own pin, so a session flips between rows with no failure (fleet-ops#9015). LiteLLM v1.98.0 never reads a redis_url under general_settings. router_settings.allowed_fails_policy.NotFoundErrorAllowedFails must be 0 (fleet-ops#9469): a 404 is a withdrawn free model or a dead model id, and the per-exception threshold falls back to the router-level allowed_fails (1) for a key the policy does not name, so without it a dead lane needs two 404s to park and leaks one to the next caller. See the allowed_fails_policy property for the mechanism and for what the 404 cooldown costs on the 7 quota-walled rows.

then.$comment: A tether row without its fallback would leave Tether unanswered on any Claude failure (Nish 2026-10-22: any Claude failure falls through to assistant).

seniorRow.$comment: fleet-ops#10040, widened 2026-10-28: a senior row is GLM-5.3-Flash on one of the two paid plans that serve it (Synthetic, the z.ai Coding Plan; Command Code's prepaid balance is empty, fleet-ops#9879). One one-slot row queued every workflow-edit review behind it, and Synthetic ends 2026-11-12 (fleet-ops#10530). Pinned so a weaker model or another provider cannot take the senior seat unreviewed.

tetherRow.$comment: Tether's Claude Sonnet 5.5 row (Nish 2026-10-22, fleet-ops#9980; 2026-10-23, Nishfleet/tether#7). The group, the model and the key are pinned together: the tether group answers only from claude-sonnet-5-5 on the Anthropic key, and that key serves no other group, so no routing group or fallback other than tether reaches the prepaid credit. The row carries a 50 USD/day wall (Nish 2026-10-23), and raising it is a deliberate change with its own issue. A caller holding the proxy master key can still name the group, so Tether's own virtual key is the only key that should list it.

judgePaidRow.$comment: fleet-ops#9374: the paid row, on the Token Plan's own numbers. rpm and max_parallel_requests are what the plan allows (3 per minute, 3 at once); neither was raised when the row became the judge primary, and raising either is a deliberate change with its own issue, not an edit to this file. model, api_base and api_key pin the seat, so a judge row cannot point the order-1 rung at another provider or spend another seat's key. fleet-ops#9405: extra_body.enable_thinking and extra_body.thinking_budget 2048 are required, because without a thinking budget this row spent the whole completion on reasoning and returned an empty body on a 40 KB diff. Sibling keys on the row never reach the DashScope compatible-mode endpoint (LiteLLM only forwards them through extra_body), so the pair lives here, not as litellm_params siblings and not as pi samplingParams.

judgeFallbackRow.$comment: fleet-ops#9374: whatever else answers a judge call answers after the paid row, never beside it, and it is an OpenCode Go row on the OpenCode Go key. The paid row duplicated as an order-2 fallback would pass a count-only rule and quietly keep judge traffic on the one seat the fallback exists to take off.

judgeFallbackKey1.$comment: fleet-ops#9374: the first OpenCode Go fallback, down to the key. Two rows on one key are one fallback with two names: a key limit or a ban on it takes both at once, which is what the second key is for.

retryPolicy.$comment: fleet-ops#9375: in-router retries must not re-send a worker prompt to a different seat more than the fallback needs. The values are locked by tests/test_router_retry_policy_no_cross_seat.py: shipped (2,2,2) produced a third in-group pick that re-sent the whole prompt cold; proposed (0,1,1) caps the worker group at one attempt before the fallback group (or Pi's own retry, which keeps the session id and therefore the pin). On litellm 1.98.0 the one allowed retry goes back to the row that just failed when that row is still healthy after the 429 (router allowed_fails 1; the test drills it). A row that parks on its first 429 (RateLimitErrorAllowedFails 0, the daily-quota rows) is already cooling, so its retry goes to a peer: still capped at one extra pick, not a same-row retry. Either way the cap removes the third-seat re-send. A litellm upgrade can change that, which is why the test pins the version. ContentPolicyViolationErrorRetries is 0 because a content-policy refusal repeats on every seat; AuthenticationErrorRetries is 0 because a bad key can never recover on retry. TimeoutErrorRetries/InternalServerErrorRetries/BadRequestErrorRetries are capped at 1 (InternalServerErrorRetries is inert on 1.98.0: get_num_retries_from_retry_policy has no InternalServerError branch, so it was a forward bound only, and it went live with the v1.105.0 image move (fleet-ops#10071). fleet-ops#9050 adds NotFoundErrorRetries and DefaultRetries, both live on 1.105.0: the policy is read before should_retry_this_error, NotFoundErrorRetries covers a status-404 answer, and DefaultRetries covers every class the policy does not name (a 402 maps to APIError with no named key; a 403 from an openai-compatible provider arrives as BadRequestError carrying status 403, which BadRequestErrorRetries already granted on both 1.98.0 and 1.105.0). Whether the granted retry reaches a different row depends on rotation: a 404 parks the row on NotFoundErrorAllowedFails 0, so the retry went to a live peer; a 403 cools nothing, so the session pin overrides the skip list and the granted attempt re-picks the same row (both drilled on 1.105.0 in tests/test_router_retry_policy_no_cross_seat.py). Both are capped at 1 like the other retry keys; named keys keep precedence, so 401/content-policy stay 0 and a 429 gets the second, peer-row retry. RateLimitErrorRetries is 2 (fleet-ops#10178: the second retry runs after the pinned row is parked and lands on a peer, so a one-slot row that is full does not leak a 429 from a group with no fallback). All keys are required and unknown keys are forbidden on purpose: a new litellm knob must arrive as a reviewed schema change, not a silent config edit.

allOf.$comment: fleet-ops#10040: one or two senior rows, every one a seniorRow (GLM-5.3-Flash on a paid plan). A missing row, a third row or a weaker model fails here.

fleet-ops#9788: Straitly is free credit only (balance 20 USD, no top-up). At most two rows, each capped at 9.5 USD, so the rows together stop routing at 19 USD and Straitly never answers 402 quota_exceeded, which LiteLLM v1.98.0 neither retries nor cools. A third row would raise the ceiling past the balance.

fleet-ops#9596: 12 parallel calls on the Synthetic key gave 8x200 and 4x429 "Too many concurrent requests", so its rows hold one slot each and at most 8 rows exist: 7 worker rows and the senior row sit at the measured working concurrency. A new Synthetic row has to take a slot from an existing one, which removes a row and needs Nish's yes (config header, Nish 2026-10-02).

Tether's Claude row: every row named tether is the pinned row, every row on the Anthropic key is a tether row, and there is at most one of each, so a second tether row, a tether row on another model or provider, or the Anthropic key on another group all fail here. Absence is allowed (the schema's own reject cases are built without it); router_settings.fallbacks requires tether -> assistant whenever the row exists.

fleet-ops#9374: the judge group used to shuffle all three rows, so the paid Alibaba Token Plan seat answered 22 of 1,054 judge calls in 14 days to 2026-10-07 while both OpenCode Go rows carried the traffic - the same family the builders use, which memory grader-never-builder-family forbids for the grader. Exactly three judge rows: one paid row on order 1 and the two fallbacks on order 2. LiteLLM v1.98.0 keeps only the lowest order group (utils._get_order_filtered_deployments) and applies that filter after the cooldown filter (router.py), so the paid row answers every judge call and the pair answers while it is cooled - measured 200/200 and 200/100 on the real Router, with every row back on order 1 spreading 30/40/30. A fourth judge row, a third order-1 row, or the fallbacks on order 1 all fail here.

the named OpenCode Go fallback row, present exactly once and on order 2, so a third judge row cannot arrive by renaming or by copying it. The key-2 fallback left on 2026-10-26: Nish chose not to renew that OpenCode Go subscription.

fleet-ops#9365: a worker-group row proven unable to cache (supports_prompt_caching false) must sit at order 2, so long-session traffic stays on cache-capable rows and the false row serves only as overflow when order-1 rows are in cooldown.

Every worker row carries an integer weight >= 1 (Nish 2026-10-13 asked for more traffic on the unlimited ds41flash rows). LiteLLM v1.98.0 simple_shuffle.py:43-46 turns weighted picking on only when the FIRST healthy row of the group has a weight, and reads a missing weight as 0: one worker row without it either switches the weighting off or gives that row a 0 share (a bench the header forbids). A weight of 0 or below is the same bench, so the floor is 1.

fleet-ops#9248: a row on openrouter.ai/api/v1 is metered by OpenRouter's free-tier DAILY quota, so its RateLimitError must park the row on the first failure. Without RateLimitErrorAllowedFails the router-level default of 1 needs a second 429, and the wall leaks to the caller: 4 of 30 parallel worker-capable calls on 2026-10-04.

fleet-ops#9788: a row on api.straitly.ai/v1 serves public-repo Pi jobs only (agent.yml picks worker-public from the repo's visibility), so it sits in worker-public. Its LiteLLM cap must trip before Straitly's own: max_budget is required and at most 9.5, and budget_duration is required because v1.98.0 registers a deployment budget only when both are set (budget_limiter._init_deployment_budgets), so a row without it has no cap at all. 30d outlasts the 2026-10-23 end date, so the budget is a lifetime cap. The prices let LiteLLM count the spend.

model_info.$comment: fleet-ops#9365: cache_proof is checked for presence and non-emptiness only, so the gate catches a missing verdict but does not read the text - 'unknown' would pass. That is deliberate: a pattern demanding a date and a token count would reject the legitimate 'cannot cache, here is the vendor doc' proof. What holds a hollow claim down is the proof line being a real measurement a reviewer can re-derive, and the probe behind it being quoted on the PR.

allowed_fails_policy.$comment: fleet-ops#9469 (PR 9472 coordinator risk): a row-level allowed_fails_policy resolves per exception type BEFORE the router policy (Router.get_allowed_fails_from_policy), so a row naming NotFoundErrorAllowedFails: 1 needs two 404s to park and re-opens the leak the router-level 0 closes. If a row names the key at all, it must be 0.

fleet-ops#9469: a 404 is a withdrawn free model or a model id that no longer exists, and it must park the row on the FIRST one. LiteLLM v1.98.0 resolves the threshold per exception type (Router.get_allowed_fails_from_policy), and a key the policy does not name falls back to the router-level allowed_fails (1) - two 404s - so a dead lane is picked again and leaks the 404 to the next caller. NotFoundErrorAllowedFails is required and pinned to 0 for that reason. The other four keys are the ones this file already sets; additionalProperties is false so a typo (NotFoundErrorAllowedFail, NotFoundErrorFails) is a rejected config rather than a silent fallback to 1. When LiteLLM adds an exception type, add its key here too - a rejection naming an unknown key is expected friction, not a bug. A row's own cooldown_time is what the 404 cooldown lasts, which is 21600 s on the 7 rows parked for a named quota wall - see config/litellm-proxy.yaml.

fallbacks.$comment: Tether: the tether entry is exactly [assistant] (a Claude failure falls to the group Hermes already uses, never to a worker group or back), and no other group may fall into tether, so the Claude credit is spent by Tether alone. fleet-ops#10040: senior is one row and has no fallback, so no entry may be keyed senior or name senior-backup (no such group exists), which also keeps judge -> senior from cycling. W10c: worker-capable is the strong group and never falls down, so no worker-capable entry may name worker-cheap, worker-public or assistant; a strong call with no healthy row fails at the caller.

optional_pre_call_checks.description: Must contain session_affinity. Without that pre-call check the router never runs DeploymentAffinityCheck, so a session pin cannot exist, every call in a session shuffles across vendors and the prompt cache never hits (fleet-ops#9361).
